American rapper [Kendrick Lamar](Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar") has released five [studio albums](Studio_album "Studio album"), one [compilation album](Compilation_album "Compilation album"), one [extended play](Extended_play "Extended play") (EP), five [mixtapes](Mixtape "Mixtape"), 65 [singles](Single_(music) "Single (music)") (including 44 as a featured artist), and three [promotional singles](Promotional_single "Promotional single"). He gained major attention after the release of his fourth mixtape *[Overly Dedicated](Overly_Dedicated "Overly Dedicated")*, which was released in 2010. It was Lamar's first full-length project to be released under his birth name and fared well enough to enter the United States *[Billboard](Billboard_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")* [Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums](Top_R%26B/Hip-Hop_Albums "Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums") chart, where it peaked at number 72.[[1]](Kendrick_Lamar_discography#cite_note-US-R&B-albums-1)

Lamar's debut studio album *<Section.80>*, was released on July 2, 2011, and issued on independent record label [Top Dawg Entertainment](Top_Dawg_Entertainment "Top Dawg Entertainment") (TDE). It peaked at number 113 on the US [*Billboard* 200](Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") chart.[[2]](Kendrick_Lamar_discography#cite_note-US-albums-2) The album's [lead single](Lead_single "Lead single"), "<HiiiPoWeR>", was released prior to the album through [iTunes](ITunes "ITunes"). The album received universal critical acclaim and reached number two on the *Billboard* 200.[[2]](Kendrick_Lamar_discography#cite_note-US-albums-2)

On March 16, 2015, Lamar released his third studio album, *[To Pimp a Butterfly](To_Pimp_a_Butterfly "To Pimp a Butterfly")*. ***Section.80*** is the debut studio album by American rapper [Kendrick Lamar](Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar"). It was released on July 2, 2011, by [Top Dawg Entertainment](Top_Dawg_Entertainment "Top Dawg Entertainment") (TDE). In the years leading up to its release, Lamar previously produced various [mixtapes](Mixtape "Mixtape") under the [moniker](Nickname "Nickname") K.Dot. In 2010, Lamar released *[Overly Dedicated](Overly_Dedicated "Overly Dedicated")*, his fourth solo [mixtape](Mixtape "Mixtape"). Shortly after its release, he began working on *Section.80*.

The [production](Hip_hop_production "Hip hop production") of *Section.80* was mainly handled by TDE in-house producers from production group [Digi+Phonics](Digi%2BPhonics "Digi+Phonics"), as well as THC, [Tommy Black](Tommy_Black_(producer) "Tommy Black (producer)"), <Wyldfyer>, [Terrace Martin](Terrace_Martin "Terrace Martin") and [J. Cole](J._Cole "J. Cole"). A [concept album](Concept_album "Concept album"), it features lyrical themes delivered by Lamar such as the 1980s [crack epidemic](Crack_epidemic "Crack epidemic"), racism and the [medication tolerance](Drug_tolerance "Drug tolerance") of [Generation Y](Millennials "Millennials"). The album features [guest appearances](Guest_appearance "Guest appearance") from [GLC](GLC_(rapper) "GLC (rapper)"), Colin Munroe, [Ashtrobot](Ash_Riser "Ash Riser"), [BJ the Chicago Kid](BJ_the_Chicago_Kid "BJ the Chicago Kid"), [Schoolboy Q](Schoolboy_Q "Schoolboy Q"), <Ab-Soul> and vocals from late singer-songwriter Alori Joh.

*Section.80* received generally positive reviews from critics upon its release. The album debuted at number 113 on the US [*Billboard* 200](Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") and as of February 2014, it has sold 130,000 copies domestically. In April 2017, it was certified [gold](RIAA_certification "RIAA certification") by the [Recording Industry Association of America](Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA).

## Background

Prior to the album's release, [Kendrick Lamar](Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar") released various mixtapes under the K.Dot [moniker](Nickname "Nickname"). The first of these [mixtapes](Mixtape "Mixtape"), titled *Youngest Head Nigga in Charge*, landed Lamar a [recording contract](Recording_contract "Recording contract") with [Top Dawg Entertainment](Top_Dawg_Entertainment "Top Dawg Entertainment").[[2]](Section.80#cite_note-2) Through Top Dawg Entertainment, Lamar would release four mixtapes, including *[Overly Dedicated](Overly_Dedicated "Overly Dedicated")*. Lamar felt compelled to create the album after seeing a friend of his go to jail for twenty-five years and experiencing the pain of such an event.[[3]](Section.80#cite_note-:0-3)

## Recording

Lamar began working on the album sometime in January 2011.[[4]](Section.80#cite_note-:1-4) The album was recorded at Top Dawg Studios in [Carson, California](Carson%2C_California "Carson, California"). Most of the album was written in Lamar's mother's kitchen and his tour bus.[[4]](Section.80#cite_note-:1-4)[[5]](Section.80#cite_note-interview-5) While recording the album, Lamar wished for it to be "as organic as possible,"[[3]](Section.80#cite_note-:0-3) at times leaving songs unfinished for extended periods of time.[[3]](Section.80#cite_note-:0-3)

***Mr. Morale & the Big Steppers*** is the fifth studio album by American rapper [Kendrick Lamar](Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar"), released on May 13, 2022, by <PGLang>, [Top Dawg Entertainment](Top_Dawg_Entertainment "Top Dawg Entertainment") (TDE), [Aftermath Entertainment](Aftermath_Entertainment "Aftermath Entertainment"), and [Interscope Records](Interscope_Records "Interscope Records"). The album serves as his first release under his creative collective PGLang, and his final project with TDE.

*Mr. Morale & the Big Steppers* is a [concept album](Concept_album "Concept album") that analyzes and reflects on his life experiences during his [therapy](Psychotherapy "Psychotherapy") journey.
